acceptance: Local and hosted metadata schemas support restart, schema upgrades, concurrent readers/writers and tenant isolation.

positive.fixture: restart after kill, v1 to v2 upgrade keeping data, concurrent readers and writers, tenant-scoped rows on SQLite; the same schema on a real temporary PostgreSQL cluster with row-level security

negative.fixture: drifted and too-new migrations refused, cross-tenant artifact links and roots refused by composite keys, tenant RLS hides other tenants, concurrent root claims succeed exactly once, drift on the PostgreSQL schema refused

versions.primitive: Schema 2 adds manifest parents and annotations; migrations are numbered, checksummed and immutable.

security_and_source_permissions: Row-level security trusts the data layer to set the tenant; it does not defend against a compromised application process.
performance_memory_storage: Not measured at this task; see T03.
known_limitations: The PostgreSQL leg is tested at the SQL level; no Go driver is added until the hosted service exists (B15)
